subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
subcategory: Privacy Laws That Changed the World
title: Biometric Privacy Laws
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Biometric Privacy Laws.

hook.text: Your fingerprint, face, and iris are uniquely yours. If stolen, you can never change them.

buildup.text: Illinois passed BIPA in 2008, requiring consent before companies collect fingerprints or face scans.

discovery.text: Facebook paid $650 million to settle a BIPA lawsuit for scanning faces in photos without consent.

twist.text: Only a handful of US states have biometric privacy laws. Most people have zero legal protection.

climax.text: Biometric data is the most permanent identifier you have. Laws protecting it are still rare.

punchline.text: Your face can't be reset. Few laws protect it.

quiz.question: Why is biometric data considered especially sensitive?
options: Unlike passwords, biometric identifiers can never be changed if compromised
It's only used by government agencies
Biometric data is already protected everywhere
